payload.title: clicking a suggestion selects it and enables submit
payload.errorMessage:
locator.waitFor: Error: strict mode violation: getByRole('combobox') resolved to 2 elements:
    1) <input value="" type="text" role="combobox" class="ae-input" aria-controls="rel-picker-listbox" aria-labelledby="rel-picker-label"/> aka getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Character' })
    2) <select name="rel_group" class="ae-select">…</select> aka getByLabel('Grouping')

Call log:
  - waiting for getByRole('combobox') to be visible

note: Modeled on a live misclassification: the judge called this REAL_BUG on one run and SELECTOR_DRIFT — correctly — on another run of the identical test the same night. A strict-mode 'resolved to N elements' error is a distinct failure signature from the timeout/absence shape the existing ambiguity rules (1-3) cover, and the taxonomy had no guidance for it. The two elements here are a text input (the intended autocomplete) and a native <select>, which the accessibility tree assigns an IMPLICIT 'combobox' role by spec — not a UI defect, not a renamed/duplicated element, just an under-scoped locator. domSnippet shows both are legitimate, differently-purposed controls (distinct accessible names 'Character' vs 'Grouping'), which is the tell that this is a selector-scoping problem: the fix is naming the locator (getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Character' })), not app code. This case exists to test whether the judge treats a multi-match strict-mode violation as ambiguous-until-shown-otherwise the same way it already treats absence.
